objectives.text: Hold the EU-Mercosur partnership on course: Uruguay ratified it on 26 February 2026, and the interim trade part has applied provisionally since 1 May 2026 with Argentina and Uruguay as the ratifying members. The deal is the market Montevideo needs beyond China and the one Brazil and Argentina share with it.

objectives.text: Sell beef and other goods to China on better terms: the government in 2023 sought a bilateral free trade agreement with Beijing, because Uruguayan beef faced a 12% tariff there against 0% for New Zealand. Orsi's own line on China was not read in this card; the sourced push is from the Lacalle Pou government, and its continuation under Orsi is our reading (C).

means.text: Beef, soy and pulp as the export base. In 2021 Uruguay exported a record US$9.8 billion; beef was 45% of that, cellulose and timber 13%, soybeans 12%, and China took US$2.7 billion (28%). In 2022 China took 27% of Uruguay's exports, two-thirds of it beef (UN Comtrade, as reported by The Cattle Site).

grand_strategy.reading: Uruguay is a small, open economy that sells beef, cellulose and soy mostly to China and depends on Mercosur for its legal frame and for the EU deal that the bloc signed together. Its strategy since 2022 has been to push the bloc towards flexibility so that it can sign its own China deal, and Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay have answered by opposing it. This card rests on tier 3 and 4 sources; the Orsi government's own line on China and on the United States was not read, and the US partner row is a gap logged in the JOURNAL.

stances.note: Uruguay cooperates inside the bloc and resists its rules at once: it wanted members allowed to pursue bilateral deals, the 2022 Asuncion summit ended with no joint declaration signed by all members, and Argentina asked Uruguay to act as a bloc. Reluctant partner is the reading of the source (a member pushing for flexibility it does not have), not our judgement. Trend cooling is our reading (C) from the 2022 summit and the November 2023 warning of measures. Bond affinity: founding member and shared bloc, no kinship. The Mercosur membership itself is a dataset row.

stances.note: Transactional. In November 2023 Lacalle Pou and Li Qiang upgraded the ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership and committed to a bilateral free trade agreement, after a completed feasibility study (reported from a Reuters story). Partner, not reluctant: no source calls the relation reluctant. Trend warming is our reading (C): the upgrade and the 12% beef tariff as the driver. Bond none: pure trade interest, no kinship. Orsi's China line was not read here, so the trend stops at the last sourced move.

stances.note: Mercosur partner, the two on the same bloc and the same river, with Portuguese and Spanish apart. Partner, not reluctant: no source reads the relation as reluctant. Trend stable is our reading (C); in 2022 Brazil's trade secretary asked for more bloc flexibility and called whether Brazil would allow the Uruguayan China move a technical question, to be decided later (the Brazilian side, not a Uruguayan reading). Brazil's 2026 disputes with Argentina are not carried here. Bond affinity: shared region and bloc, no kinship. Since is the July 2022 Asuncion summit, the first dated position read.

The sourced friction is from 2022, when President Fernandez criticised Uruguay's bilateral move and asked it to act as the whole bloc, and from the November 2023 joint warning of measures; the Milei-Orsi distance itself is not read in a Uruguayan source here and is not written as a fact. Joint ratification of the EU deal in February 2026 is the shared ground. Partner, not reluctant: no source calls it reluctant. Trend cooling is our reading (C). Bond kin is our reading (C), from the shared language and the Rio de la Plata; no source read on identity.
